dedupe_keys.name: hifda high frequency electrical voltage and current signals from household appliances

description: HIFDA - High-Frequency Electrical Voltage and Current Signals from Household Appliances is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Víctor M. Navarro et al. The increasing demand for efficient energy management in smart grids has led to the development of various Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) techniques. These aim to disaggregate energy consumption and classify appliances using data from a single-point smart meter at a household’s grid mains. With the use of machine learning methods, NILM solutions increasingly rely on datasets for training and validation. Coverage: a single site or case study; published in 2025. Formats: TXT, ZIP. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support power-system, energy-planning and grid-operation studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
